Subject (in full) Japanese bomber reported to have crashed near
Point Island.

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

With reference to the translation attached which
appeared in the "Ta Kung Pao" newspaper on December 9, 1937,
enquiries made through Yangtsepoo Station and the U.S.
marine authorities who maintain a guard at the Shanghai
Power Company's Yangtsepoo Plant fail to confirm any such
incident as a Japanese bomber crashing on Point Island at
7 a.m. on December 8, 1937. An explosion, which is
confirmed by the above sources, did occur at 7 a.m. December
8, but as far as can be ascertained was caused through the
igniting and destruction of a gasoline storage tank.
Information as to the cause is not available.

Ta Kung Pao Urges China To
Co-operate With Foreign
Powers Hostile To Japan

Continuance Of Diplomatic And Economic
Relations With Tokyo Is Declared
Ridiculous By Chinese Paper

Diplomatically, there are now only three courses open to China in the face of Japan's continued aggression, declared the Ta Kung Pao, a leading Chinese daily newspaper here, in an editorial yesterday.
The three courses, the journal enumerated, are: (1) to yield to the Japanese military pressure by accepting Japan's overture to sign a joint anti-Comintern pact; (2) to pursue a dilatory policy similar to that adopted after the Mukden incident; and (3) to openly co-operate with Powers hostile to Japan.

Will Not Surrender
The first course, the paper believed, is not acceptable to China, as she is determined not to surrender to Japan, thereby exposing Soviet Russia to the Japanese menace. This determined stand was clearly stated by Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek in his message on the eve of China's Independence Day.
"It is also impossible," the journal added, "for China to take the second course since Japan is bent upon subjugating China by military force. She would never cease her military operations, unless China accepts humiliating terms that the aggressor may dictate".
"As to the last course which appears to be possible at this moment, present tendencies indicate that China is still wavering in her decision. It is imperative, however, that China should clarify her stand without further loss of time."

Abnormal Situation
The Ta Kung Pao considered ridiculous the fact that China still maintains her diplomatic and economic relations with Japan in the midst of the present undeclared war which has all the elements of a major conflict between two countries. This abnormal situation, it opined, only serves to show the world that China is not carrying on her defensive war with a firm determination.
The journal urged that efforts should be made to win sympathy and help from Powers which are friendly to China and that a definite foreign policy be adopted to guide the task of national salvation, Central News reports.

本社讯，当地主要中文日报《大公报》昨日发表社论宣称，面对日本的持续侵略，中国在外交上现在只有三条路可走。
该报列举的这三条路是：(1) 接受日本提出的签署共同防共协定的提议，屈服于日本的军事压力；(2) 采取类似九一八事变后所采用的拖延政策；以及 (3) 公开与敌视日本的列强合作。

不会投降
该报认为，第一条路是中国不能接受的，因为中国决心不向日本投降，从而使苏俄暴露在日本的威胁之下。蒋介石委员长在中国国庆日前夕的文告中明确阐述了这一坚定立场。
该报补充道：“中国也不可能走第二条路，因为日本一心要用武力征服中国。除非中国接受侵略者可能强加的屈辱条款，否则日本绝不会停止军事行动。”
“至于目前看来可行的最后一条路，目前的迹象表明中国在决策上仍在犹豫。然而，中国必须毫不拖延地澄清其立场。”

异常情况
《大公报》认为，在目前这场具有两国间重大冲突所有要素的未宣战战争中，中国仍与日本保持外交和经济关系，这一事实是荒谬的。该报认为，这种异常情况只会向世界表明，中国并非以坚定的决心进行防御战。
据中央通讯社报道，该报敦促努力争取友好国家对中国的同情和帮助，并采取明确的外交政策来指导救国任务。

MANY CASUALTIES CAUSED IN THE SETTLEMENT BY RECKLESS
ACTIVITIES OF JAPANESE PLANES

During the past few days Japanese planes
have recklessly bombed Chapei, Nantao and Pootung and
frequently machine-gunned non-combatants such as refugees
and rescue workers of charitable societies.
Small type hand grenades were dropped from
Japanese planes while flying over the Settlement area
yesterday afternoon, killing and wounding a number of
innocent civilians.
Between 6.30 a.m. and 7 a.m. to-day, while
a squadron of Japanese planes were flying over the Settlement,
bombs and other explosives began to fall in many parts of the
area and machine-gun fire was also poured onto many other
places, inflicting a number of casualties. Ambulances
busily answered the calls whilst the Chinese Lester, Paulun
and other hospitals were crowded with wounded persons.
The following are some of the cases that have
been known :-
(1) Five persons were injured at the corner
of Chekiang and Ningpo Roads.
(2) One person was wounded on Tientsin Road
near Chekiang Road.
(3) More than 10 persons were wounded at the
corner of Nanking and Yunnan Roads.
(4) Two killed and three others wounded on
Tansui Road.
(5) Many persons were wounded on Bubbling
Well Road in the vicinity of the Park Hotel.
(6) One ticket inspector of the Tramway
Company was injured at Avenue Haig terminus.
(7) Two children were injured at the entrance
to the Dah Chung Li (大中華), Yates Road.
The roof of the Chengtu Road Police Station
was also hit by a stray shell at 6.50 a.m. to-day, but
fortunately no one was hurt.

日军飞机肆意活动致租界多人伤亡

过去几天，日军飞机肆意轰炸闸北、南市和浦东，并频繁用机枪扫射难民和慈善团体的救援人员等非战斗人员。
昨天下午，日军飞机在飞越租界区域时投掷小型手榴弹，造成多名无辜平民死伤。
今天上午6时30分至7时之间，当一队日军飞机飞越租界上空时，炸弹和其他爆炸物开始落在该区域的许多地方，机枪火力也倾泻到许多其他地方，造成多人伤亡。救护车忙于出警，而中式莱斯特医院（Lester Hospital）、宏仁医院（Paulun Hospital）和其他医院挤满了伤者。
以下是已知的一些案例：
(1) 浙江路与宁波路拐角处五人受伤。
(2) 天津路靠近浙江路处一人受伤。
(3) 南京路与云南路拐角处十余人受伤。
(4) 淡水路两人死亡，三人受伤。
(5) 国际饭店附近的静安寺路多人受伤。
(6) 海格路终点站一名电车公司查票员受伤。
(7) 亚达路（Yates Road）大中华里（Dah Chung Li）入口处两名儿童受伤。
今天上午6时50分，成都路巡捕房的屋顶也被一枚流弹击中，但幸运的是无人受伤。

Mr. Yao Sin-noon (姚辛農) having drafted
the manifesto to be issued after the meeting, it was then
revised and made public. Mr. Lu Choh-ngoo (魯卓吾) of
the Central Educational Films Association made the following
suggestions:-
(1) That the manifesto be translated into
English and French.
(2) That a telegram be sent to the
Executive Yuan and the Shanghai City Government.
(3) That a letter be sent to the S.M.C.,
the Chinese members of the Council and the Chinese
Ratepayers' Association.
The suggestions were accepted.
Mr. Yao Sin-noon held the opinion that
a telegram should be sent to Britain, America and France
reporting the illegal censorship of films and dramas
by the Settlement authorities in Shanghai.
At this time, someone present remarked:
"The resistance against invasion has been commenced in
North China. In the name of the meeting, a telegram of
encouragement should be sent to the officers and men
of the 29th Army. Ostensibly, it has nothing to do with
the meeting, but as a matter of fact, the so-called
Settlement Film and Dramatic Censors are the 'running dogs'
of the Japanese. Therefore, the matters of offering
resistance against and bringing about the abolition of the
Settlement Film and Dramatic Censorship cannot be separated
from each other."
The majority of those present were in
agreement with the above suggestion. The telegram of
encouragement was at once drafted and is believed to have
been sent on July 12.
Others said: "A few days ago, many youths
were illegally arrested by the Settlement authorities in
the Bund Garden on the ground that they were singing
patriotic songs. Since this Committee aims at the abolition
of the Settlement Film and Dramatic Censorship, we should
express our opinion regarding this case."
The point was discussed and the meeting
passed a resolution that lawyers be retained to call at
the Police Station to console the arrested youths; that
a letter be sent to the Chinese Ratepayers' Association
asking it to open negotiations for their release.
Mr. Chow Chien-yuin (周建雲) made the
following report: "On the evening of July 9, some 100
people in cultural circles held a dinner party at Dinty
Moore's Restaurant, during which it was resolved to form
a 'Chinese National Salvation Association'. It is strange
that no reports regarding this meeting appeared in Chinese
newspapers, but Japanese newspapers have published this
news, as traitors were present that evening! In future,
we must guard against this."
The meeting terminated at 8 p.m.

Ta Kung Pao (May 19) :-

CORRECTION

Recently, local newspapers published a report to the effect that officers of the Zau Ka Doo Branch Police Bureau had, by means of torture, caused the death of Chow Ah-ping (周阿平), a worker of the Dah Hwa Leather Factory (大華製革廠). An investigation from various sources concerned shows that the report is untrue.

Chow Ah-ping was a worker of the Dah Hwa Leather Factory. He was arrested first by Hongkew Police Station when he was bringing a motor, that he had stolen from the factory, to the Settlement for the purpose of selling it. Upon questioning, it was learned that the crime was committed in Chinese territory. Hongkew Station then informed the Detective Squad of the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau by telephone and an officer was sent to take over the prisoner. Chow Ah-ping was brought before the Shanghai District Court and charged. Later he was released from the Court on security and died in his home. At no time did the Zau Ka Doo Branch Police Bureau or the Detective Squad attached to the Branch Bureau handle the case. Therefore, the report appearing in the local newspapers to the effect that the case was under investigation of the Zau Ka Doo Branch Police Bureau is absolutely groundless.

According to press reports of May 18, a certain public officer was detained when the case was heard at the Shanghai District Court, but according to a certain responsible official of the Police Bureau, no such case has taken place in which a police officer has been detained.

Ta Kung Pao publishes the following article written by one
Chiang Moo Liang ( 蔣牧良 ) :- 27-1-37 (P.M.)

"I HAVE FAILED"

It was a snowy night and dark. The
sky above Nanking Road and vicinity is reddened by the
Neon lights.

Zang Zi Sz ( 尚席儒 ) ran out from a
public lavatory upon being chased by a policeman. He
had no place where he could go to pass the night. As
he was thinking about something, he suddenly heard a
sound behind him; he turned and found a tall policeman
running fiercely towards him. He took to his heels.
"Where can I find a place to sleep?"
he said to himself. "I am very foolish. Why should I
have run away just now? Let him take me to the Police
Station where I can pass the night. I could
have saved myself from suffering in such a night of
wind and snow. It is said that the Police requires
every policeman to have at least 8 cases a month, failing
which he would be punished. A poor man like me is
liable to be arrested by policemen even when walking
properly on the streets for policemen want cases. If
I were urinate or have a movement of the bowels on the
street, it would settle the question."

Zang Zi Sz then went to the intersection
of two streets and saw a policeman standing under the
signal lights. He walked to a place about 10 feet to
20 feet from the policeman where he began to urinate.
At first, the face of the policeman was towards him,
but when the man began to urinate, the policeman turned
and pretended not to see him.
"Let me have a movement of the bowels
here", the man said. He crouched down on the ground,
exposing his buttocks to the wind.
A sound of steps approached. The man
was not frightened.
The policeman said, "Are you mad?
You cannot move your bowels here".
"I am in a hurry and cannot help it",
answered the man.
The policeman slapped his face and
kicked him with his booted feet. The man fell to the
ground and vomited blood.

"Why do you assault me? If I have violated
the regulations, why do you not take me to the Police
Station? Why do you assault me?"
"You want me to take you to the Police
Station. You are too poor to find a place to live in
and try to make the Police Station your lodging house.
Do you think that I do not know about this? I shall
beat the life out of you".
The man was again kicked.
"To-day is the 3rd day of the month and
I am in no hurry to have a case. I shall beat the life
out of you."
The man took up his trousers and ran away
as fast as he could. He again vomitted some blood and
then collapsed, saying, "I have failed, I have failed".

《大公报》刊登一篇由蒋牧良（Chiang Moo Liang）撰写的文章：- 1937年1月27日（下午）

“我失败了”

那是一个下雪的夜晚，天色漆黑。南京路及附近地区的天空被霓虹灯映得通红。

尚席儒（Zang Zi Sz）被一名警察追赶，从公共厕所跑了出来。他无处过夜。当他正在思索时，突然听到身后有声音；他转身发现一名高大的警察正凶猛地向他跑来。他拔腿就跑。
“我去哪里找个地方睡觉呢？”他自言自语道。“我真蠢。刚才为什么要跑？让他把我带到警察局，我就可以在那里过夜了。我本可以免受这风雪之夜的痛苦。据说警方要求每名警察每月至少办理8起案件，否则就会受到处罚。像我这样的穷人，即使在街上正常行走也容易被警察逮捕，因为警察需要案件。如果我在街上小便或大便，问题就解决了。”

尚席儒随后走到一个十字路口，看见一名警察站在信号灯下。他走到距离警察约10到20英尺的地方开始小便。起初，警察的脸朝着他，但当那人开始小便时，警察转过身去，假装没看见他。
“让我在这里大便吧”，那人说。他蹲在地上，臀部暴露在风中。
脚步声靠近。那人并不害怕。
警察说：“你疯了吗？你不能在这里大便”。
“我很急，没办法”，那人回答。
警察扇了他一耳光，并用穿着靴子的脚踢他。那人倒在地上，吐出血来。

“你为什么打我？如果我违反了规定，你为什么不把我带到警察局？你为什么打我？”
“你想让我把你带到警察局。你太穷了，找不到住的地方，想把警察局当作旅馆。你以为我不知道这一点吗？我要把你打死”。
那人又被踢了一脚。
“今天是月初三号，我不急着要案件。我要把你打死”。
那人提起裤子，尽可能快地跑开了。他又吐了一些血，然后瘫倒在地，说道：“我失败了，我失败了”。

The National Herald:

JAPAN PURCHASING HUGE QUANTITIES OF RICE

In order to be stocked with supplies in case
of war, Japan has purchased a large quantity of Chinese
rice and wheat this year. During the past few months,
about 20,000 bags of rice have been purchased by Japan from
Shanghai, Tsingpoo, Sungkiang and other places.
Yesterday the Hsin Chong, the Van Shing and the
Tsing Tai Rice Hongs at Ter Shih Ka (芝市街), Nantab, loaded
3,000 bags of rice on a ship on behalf of rice hongs of

Shanghai Pao (上海報) publishes the following comment :-

SAFETY IN THE FOREIGN SETTLEMENTS

According to a responsible census officer, more
than 25,000 people had removed from Chapei to the Settlement
during the tense local situation. The western district
is regarded as the safest place in times of trouble, but
in our opinion, this is only imagination, because in case
of war, the heavy artillery can reach every corner of
Shanghai; furthermore, according to treaties, a Settlement
is only a piece of territory leased to foreigners wherein
the jurisdiction over Chinese residents is still vested
in the Chinese authorities. From this, it can be seen that
it is only natural that the S.M.C. should decline to accept
responsibility for the safety of residents in the Settlement,
as can be verified by the statement made by Mr. Fessenden,
Secretary-General of the S.M.C., to the effect that the
S.M.C. has no right to open negotiations for the cessation
of the movements and activities of the Japanese landing
forces in the Settlement. This statement clarified the
present position of the Settlement. We hope that our
fellow countrymen will not be so foolish as to think that
the Settlement is a place of safety to which they could
rush for shelter in case of hostilities.

World Morning News (世界晨報) (comment):-

THE CASE AGAINST THE "TA KUNG PAO"

The other day Chang Chi Luan (張季鸞), editor
of the "Ta Kung Pao", was prosecuted by the Shanghai
Municipal Council for publishing an article which was
considered to be contrary to the "good relations" order
issued by the Chinese Government. The Court found Chang
not guilty on the ground that "Manchukuo" was not
recognized as a State by China. If we remember aright,
"Manchukuo" has not only been unrecognized by China, but
by all the Powers (except Japan) represented on the Consular
Body, the superior organ of the Shanghai Municipal Council.
Then how did the Shanghai Municipal Council come to
misunderstand the "good relations" order? We may attribute
it to the failure of China to recover the lost land.

《上海报》发表如下评论：-

租界之安全

据一位负责的户籍官员称，在当地局势紧张期间，有超过25,000人从闸北迁入租界。西区被视为动荡时期的最安全之地，但在我们看来，这仅仅是想象，因为一旦开战，重炮可以覆盖上海的每一个角落；此外，根据条约，租界只是租赁给外国人的领土，对中国居民的管辖权仍属于中国当局。由此可见，工部局拒绝承担租界居民的安全责任是理所当然的，工部局秘书长费森登先生（Mr. Fessenden）的声明可证实这一点，他表示工部局无权就停止日军登陆部队在租界内的移动和行动进行谈判。这一声明澄清了租界目前的地位。我们希望我们的同胞不要愚蠢地认为，租界是一个在敌对行动发生时可以 rush 去寻求庇护的安全之地。

《世界晨报》评论：-

起诉《大公报》案

日前，《大公报》编辑张季鸾因发表一篇被认为违背中国政府发布的“睦邻”令的文章，被上海公共租界工部局起诉。法院以“满洲国”未获中国承认为国家为由，判决张无罪。如果我们记得没错，“满洲国”不仅未获中国承认，也未获驻沪领事团（上海公共租界工部局的上级机构）所代表的除日本以外的所有列强承认。那么，上海公共租界工部局为何会误解“睦邻”令呢？我们可以将其归咎于中国未能收复失地。

The Movie Star Half-Monthly (明星半月刊), Volume 6, Issues 5
and 6 combined, published the following comment:

"AN UNREASONABLE INTERFERENCE AND PROSECUTION"

The action of the S.M.C. in unreasonably
prohibiting the Zuh Nyih Small Dramatic Group (演劇小劇團)
from staging the play entitled "The Smuggling" (走私)
and other patriotic dramatic plays aroused great public
indignation. Later, the Council instituted an unreasonable
prosecution against the "Ta Kung Pao" (大公報), a local
Chinese daily, for publishing an article dealing with the
Zuh Nyi Dramatic Group affair. Such despotic action on
the part of the S.M.C. is indeed intolerable.

The people of a nation, however civilized
or barbarous they may be, are entitled to absolute freedom
to love their country and to indulge in their particular
cultural movements, because this is a sacred privilege
which cannot be interfered with, however strong or despotic
may be the influence that may be brought to bear upon it.

The S.M.C., in exercising such a strict
censorship of motion pictures and dramatic plays in the
International Settlement is already acting despotically.
The motion picture and dramatic circles have, however,
always observed the "proper and legal" procedure, and
even if this "legal procedure" and system" is of a kind
that is usually imposed upon the people of a colony, it
should be applied within certain limits. We do not know
on what ground the S.M.C. is prohibiting us from referring
to our territory in the north-east or to "Manchukuo",
a puppet state, that has not even been recognized by
the British Government.

For the sake of the prestige of our
cultural movement and our freedom to express our patriotism
by means of motion pictures or dramatic plays, cultural
bodies should lodge a strong protest with the S.M.C.
for the prosecution of the "Ta Kung Pao".

Lih Pao (立報) publishes the following comments:

THE SINO-JAPANESE RELATIONS

Bringing with him the new instructions
of the Japanese Government regarding the policy to be
adopted towards China, Mr. Kuwajima, Director of the Bureau
of East Asiatic Affairs of the Tokyo Foreign Office,
arrived at Shanghai yesterday.

According to a Domei telegram yesterday,
Premier Hirota has sought an audience with the Japanese
Emperor to submit a memorandum on the plans to be adopted

readjustment of the relations between the two countries,
close attention is being paid to the following two points:-
1) That the national prestige of the Chinese Government
be not harmed.
2) That all fears concerning the integrity of China's
territory be removed.

《明星半月刊》第6卷第5、6期合刊发表了如下评论：

“无理干涉与起诉”

工部局无理禁止“实验小剧团”上演名为《走私》及其他爱国戏剧的行为，引起了公众的极大愤慨。随后，工部局又因一家本地中文日报《大公报》刊登了一篇涉及实验剧团事件的文章，而对该报进行了无理起诉。工部局这种专制行为确实令人无法容忍。

一个国家的人民，无论文明或野蛮，都有绝对自由去热爱自己的国家并从事其特定的文化运动，因为这是一种神圣的特权，无论施加其上的影响多么强大或专制，都不得干涉。

工部局在国际租界对电影和戏剧实施如此严格的审查，本身就是在实行专制。然而，电影界和戏剧界一直遵守“正当且合法”的程序，即使这种“法律程序”和“制度”通常是强加于殖民地人民的，也应在一定限度内适用。我们不知道工部局基于什么理由禁止我们提及我国东北领土或“满洲国”这个甚至连英国政府都未承认的傀儡政权。

为了维护我们文化运动的声誉以及我们通过电影或戏剧表达爱国主义的自由，文化团体应就起诉《大公报》一事向工部局提出强烈抗议。

《立报》发表如下评论：

中日关系

东京外务省东亚局局长桑岛先生带着日本政府关于对华政策的新指示，于昨日抵达上海。

据共同社昨日电讯，广田首相已求见日本天皇，提交一份关于日本政府处理中日问题计划的备忘录。为了实现两国关系的根本调整，正密切关注以下两点：-
1) 不损害中国政府的国家威望。
2) 消除对中国领土完整的所有担忧。

MAINICHI

SPECIAL DISTRICT COURT RECOGNIZES ANTI-JAPANESE
DRAMA

When the "Ta Kung Pao"
published in its literary column an article entitled
"Plays that are banned" the Municipal Police prosecuted
Chang, the editor of the paper, on a charge of violating
the peace and good order. The hearing of the case
was held on September 19 in the First Special District
Court. The accused was acquitted.
The Municipal Police authorities
and leading Japanese circles are indignant over the
judgement. The plays in questions are "A night in
Mukden", which based on the Manchurian Incident, "Glory
of the Nation", a play which praises the work of the
19th Route Army during the Sino-Japanese hostilities
in Shanghai, and "Plays that are banned". They are
nothing but plays propagating anti-Japanese thoughts.
The reasons contained in the
judgement handed down by the Court are, briefly, as follows:-
"It is a play aimed to propagate
patriotic ideas; it has not been staged. The article
contains the expressions 'Overthrow Japanese', 'Japanese
devils' and 'Oppose Manchukuo! It also contains
anti-foreign expressions but these expressions do not
definitely refer to Japan. The three Eastern Provinces
are part of Chinese territory and the Chinese Government
still regards them as such. Therefore, there is no
reason for any one to make a complaint against matters
relating to Manchukuo."

ACTION MAY BE TAKEN AGAINST WU VOONG LING

As the girl Wu Voong Ling is
of sound mind and is insisting that her statement is
true, it is evident that some one is working behind the
scenes. The Japanese Naval Landing Party authorities
intend to take action against the girl, for the spreading
of the false report will impair the prestige of the
Imperial Navy.
It is reported that Wu Voong
Ling is not registered at any school in the Kiangwan
district. She had probably, at the instigation of the
anti-Japanese National Salvation Association, invented
the report for the sake of publicity.
On the ground that Wu is a
resident in the Settlement, the Bureau of Public Safety
evaded its responsibility. The inquiries of the
Municipal Police have been delayed because of the
allegation that the assault took place in Chinese territory.
It has now been established that the girl had made a false
statement.

《每日新闻》

特区法院认可反日戏剧

当《大公报》在其文学专栏刊登题为《被禁演的戏剧》的文章时，警务处以扰乱治安罪起诉该报编辑张氏。案件审理于9月19日在第一特区法院举行。被告被判无罪。
警务局当局和日本主要圈子对该判决感到愤怒。涉案剧目包括基于满洲事变的《沈阳之夜》，赞扬十九路军在上海中日冲突期间功绩的《民族之光》，以及《被禁演的戏剧》。它们不过是传播反日思想的戏剧。
法院判决书中的理由简要如下：-
“这是一部旨在传播爱国思想的戏剧；它并未上演。文章包含‘打倒日本’、‘日本鬼子’和‘反对满洲国！’等表述。它也包含排外表述，但这些表述并不明确指向日本。东三省是中国领土的一部分，中国政府至今仍视其为如此。因此，任何人没有理由就涉及满洲国的事项提出投诉。”

可能对吴武灵（音译）采取行动

由于女孩吴武灵（音译）神志清醒并坚持其陈述属实，显然有人在幕后操纵。日本海军陆战队当局打算对该女孩采取行动，因为散布虚假报告将损害帝国海军的威望。
据报道，吴武灵（音译）未在江湾地区的任何学校注册。她很可能是在抗日救国会的唆使下，为了宣传目的而编造了这一报道。
公安局以吴是租界居民为由推卸责任。警务处的调查因声称袭击发生在中国领土而受到延误。现已查明该女孩作了虚假陈述。

该文章是否确实构成违反促进与外国友好关系的政府命令，或者租界当局的压制是否不合理，尽管众所周知，但我们目前不便置评。我们最好等待法院的判决。此外，现在陈述此案将对文化和戏剧界产生何种影响也不合时宜。

中西药业公会和全国医药团体联合会日前举行联席会议，决议成立一个委员会来处理“拜耳”公司的问题，并建议中国药店在案件解决之前停止购买该公司的产品。

《辛报》：

“《大公报》案”

中国为促进与日本的良好关系做了大量工作，而日本也特别注意其对华关系，如下报道所示：
“一名日本海军陆战队员误用刺刀碰触了一名名叫石喜康（Shih Zay Kong）的中国人的腿部，造成轻微伤害。该陆战队员向石道歉并为其进行治疗。据工部局报告，石希望和解，因为他只受了轻伤。9月17日，日本海军当局派出一名副官慰问石”。
日本的这种态度也非常友好。然而，有些中国人坚持说东北属于中国。这导致了《大公报》因发表题为《禁演的戏》的文章而引发的案件。
起诉该报社的原告并非“友邦”成员；他是中国人。

Sin Wan Pao of September 20 published the following article contributed by one Tsai Foh Zung (蔡復誠) :-

PAPER HUNTING

During the past 15 years, foreigners have been holding paper hunts in Zau Wo Ching (曹河涇), Poo Sung (蒲淞) and Hungjao (虹橋) in the western district of Shanghai during the holidays in spring and autumn when the weather is fine. Sometimes more than 100 riders take part.

Paper hunting causes much damage to crops. After the establishment of the Shanghai City Government, the leading members of the districts submitted petitions protesting against paper hunting and requesting the City Government to suppress the hunting. The City Government opened negotiations with the various Consuls concerned, as a result of which, the Paper Hunt Club agreed to issue a grant of from $200 to $300 for damage done each year commencing from the 17th Year of the Chinese Republic (1928). The money was handed to the leading members of the districts for distribution among the peasants, but it never reached the farmers. The object of the agitation created by these leading members of the districts was to make some money and not because of their interest in the welfare of the peasants. Owing to this double dealing on the part of these persons, the farmers are still cursing the "foreign devils" for causing damage to their fields.

Iron News (鐵報) :-

THE CASE AGAINST THE "TA KUNG PAO".

The case of the S.M.C. in prohibiting the Zuh Nyi Small Dramatic Group from staging a play entitled "Smuggling" has not yet been settled.

Recently, the "Ta Kung Pao" published a one-act drama entitled "The Banned Plays"(演不出的戲) written by one Zung Bah Sen(陳白塵), which described the case of the Zuh Nyi Small Dramatic Group. The S.M.P. brought a charge against the "Ta Kung Pao" for publishing an article liable to incite the public to break the law and order, in addition to which the Police also quoted the mandate issued by the National Government ordering the people to maintain friendly relations with foreign Powers. Thus, the writer of this article seems to have incurred the displeasure of our "friendly nation" --- Manchukuo.

The performance of the play entitled "Smuggling" was banned by the S.M.C. on the ground that it contained an expression "The North-East is ours". In the case against the "Ta Kung Pao", the S.M.P. arbitrarily regards Manchukuo as a friendly nation of China. Possibly the S.M.C. will exert pressure on us until we recognize Manchukuo.

We are not citizens of a conquered nation and we shall never tolerate such unreasonable oppression and prosecution Every Chinese should lodge a strong protest against the affair.

在过去15年里，外国人在上海西区的曹河涇（Zau Wo Ching）、蒲淞（Poo Sung）和虹桥（Hungjao），于春秋两季天气晴朗的假期举行猎纸游戏。有时有超过100名骑手参加。

猎纸游戏对农作物造成很大损害。上海市政府成立后，各区领袖提交请愿书，抗议猎纸游戏，并要求市政府予以取缔。市政府与有关各国领事进行谈判，结果猎纸俱乐部同意从民国十七年（1928年）开始，每年支付200至300美元作为损害赔偿金。这笔钱交给各区领袖分发给农民，但从未到达农民手中。这些区领袖制造骚动的目的是为了捞取钱财，而非出于对农民福利的关注。由于这些人的两面派手法，农民们仍在咒骂“洋鬼子”毁坏他们的田地。

World Morning News (世界晨报) published the following comment
on September 14 :-

THE CASE AGAINST THE "TA KUNG PAO"

Recently the Shanghai Municipal Police prosecuted
the "Ta Kung Pao" for having published an article entitled
"Plays That Are Banned" which was regarded as an infringement
of the orders of the National Government for the promotion
of good relations with foreign countries. This case has
made us more angry than the case in which the S.M.P.
prohibited the Zuh Nyi (实验) Dramatic Group and the Ants
(蚂蚁) Dramatic Group from staging certain plays, because
the plays contained the expression: "The North-East is our
territory". The "Ta Kung Pao" is being prosecuted for
a true description of the facts in such incidents.
The expression "The North-East is our
territory" is not a slogan; it is a fact. Every Chinese
recognizes that the North-East is our territory and they
will never forget to recover it. This is recognized by
the Chinese Government and all foreign countries (except
Japan). Then on what ground, is the S.M.P. prosecuting
the "Ta Kung Pao"? Is it that in the eyes of policemen
and detectives, the North-East does not belong to China?
The duty of the Police is to preserve peace
and order, but its action against the staging of certain
plays and the publishing of certain articles is very strange.
We recall that on one occasion Lord Marley
brought up a question in the British House of Lords regarding
the assaulting of patriotic processionists by the S.M.P.
We feel that Lord Marley should bring up another question
in the House of Lords regarding the present two cases.
It will be interesting to see how the Court
will decide the case of the "Ta Kung Pao". In such cases
in the past, the Court used to deliver its decisions
without much thought and the accused were fined. We hope
that in this case the Court will no longer act in such a
way as to please foreigners.
The law is just, but we cannot believe that
the law will punish patriotism.

Variety Fortnightly (好乐) of September 12 :-

THE CASE OF THE BANNED PLAYS

The Mo Ni (蚂蚁) ("Ants") Dramatic Group
has been twice illegally prohibited by the S.M.C. from
staging patriotic plays. Subsequently, the Group formed
a Negotiations Committee with Zee Pu (徐普) and four
others as members, and asked lawyers Soo Chien Li (李千里)
and Yang Chien Sung (杨千松) to write to the S.M.C. about
the matter. They obtained a reply from the S.M.C. stating
that the Council's action was based on the Yangkingpang
Regulations. Contending that the Yangkingpang Regulations
had nothing to do with this matter, the Group sent a second
letter of protest. Tha S.M.C. sent a second reply, but
it contained nothing of importance.
The Group has now decided to lodge a protest
with the Consular Body.

《世界晨报》于9月14日发表如下评论：

控告《大公报》案

近日，上海公共租界工部局警务处起诉《大公报》，因其刊登了一篇题为《禁演的戏》的文章，该文章被视为违反了国民政府关于促进与外国友好关系的命令。此案比警务处禁止“实验”戏剧团和“蚂蚁”戏剧团上演某些剧目一事更令我们愤怒，因为那些剧目中包含“东北是我们的领土”这一表述。《大公报》因如实描述此类事件的事实而遭到起诉。
“东北是我们的领土”这一表述并非口号；它是一个事实。每个中国人都承认东北是我们的领土，并且永远不会忘记收复它。这一点得到了中国政府及所有外国（日本除外）的承认。那么，警务处起诉《大公报》的依据何在？难道在警察和侦探眼中，东北不属于中国吗？
警察的职责是维护和平与秩序，但其针对上演某些剧目和刊登某些文章所采取的行动却非常奇怪。
我们记得，有一次马利勋爵（Lord Marley）在英国上议院提出质询，涉及警务处殴打爱国游行人士一事。我们认为，马利勋爵应在上议院就目前的这两起案件再次提出质询。
看看法院将如何裁决《大公报》一案将是很有趣的。在过去类似的案件中，法院往往不经深思熟虑便作出判决，对被告处以罚款。我们希望在此案中，法院不再采取这种取悦外国人的做法。
法律是公正的，但我们无法相信法律会惩罚爱国主义。

9月12日的《好乐》双周刊：

禁演剧目案

“蚂蚁”戏剧团曾两次被工部局非法禁止上演爱国剧目。随后，该剧团成立了一个谈判委员会，成员包括徐普（Zee Pu，音译）等五人，并委托律师李千里（Soo Chien Li，音译）和杨千松（Yang Chien Sung，音译）就此事宜致函工部局。他们收到了工部局的回复，称工部局的行动是基于《洋泾浜章程》。剧团辩称《洋泾浜章程》与此事无关，遂发出第二封抗议信。工部局发出了第二封回复，但其中并无重要内容。
该剧团现已决定向领事团提出抗议。

September 22, 1936. Morning Translation.

Lih Pao (立报) and other local newspapers :-

THE COURT'S DECISION IN THE "TA KUNG PAO" CASE

On August 16, the "Ta Kung Pao" published an article entitled "Plays That Are Banned". On the ground that the article was liable to incite the people's feelings and constituted an infringement of the order of the National Government for the promotion of good relations with foreign countries, the S.M.P. prosecuted Chang Chi Lieu (張季鸞), Chief Editor of the paper, in the First Shanghai Special District Court. The case came up for hearing on September 10 and was remanded to September 17 when the Chief Editor of the paper was found not guilty.

The judgment handed down by the Court in the "Ta Kung Pao" case contains the following reasons :-
1) The article describes the indignation of the members of a certain dramatic group and their dissatisfaction with the ban placed on the staging of their plays. It cannot be regarded as being of a nature liable to excite the people's feelings or as a violation of the order of the Government for the promotion of good relations with foreign countries.
2) The article contains the expressions: "Overthrow the IX devils" and "Overthrow the people of a certain nation". These expressions do not definitely point to any particular friendly nation.
3) The Three Eastern Provinces are part of Chinese territory and the Chinese Government still regards them as such. Though the so-called "Manchukuo" has been established in the Three Eastern Provinces, the Chinese Government has not recognized it as a proper State. The article contains anti-"Manchukuo" expressions, but they cannot be regarded as constituting a violation of the order for the promotion of good relations with foreign countries.
4) Chang Chi Lieu is the Chief Editor of the "Ta Kung Pao" and is a busy man. He does not pay much attention to light articles in the supplement columns of his paper. If the article complained of contains improper expressions, the accused Chang is responsible for the mistake, but he cannot be regarded as having wilfully violated the Criminal Code and menaced peace and good order.

《大公报》案的法院判决

8月16日，《大公报》刊登了一篇题为《禁演的戏》的文章。警务处以该文章可能煽动民众情绪并构成违反国民政府关于促进与外国友好关系命令为由，在上海第一特区地方法院起诉该报总编辑张季鸾（Chang Chi Lieu）。该案于9月10日开庭审理，并延期至9月17日宣判，该报总编辑被判无罪。

法院在《大公报》一案中作出的判决包含以下理由：
1) 该文章描述了某戏剧团成员对禁止其上演剧目的愤慨和不满。不能认为其性质足以煽动民众情绪或违反政府关于促进与外国友好关系的命令。
2) 该文章包含“打倒九鬼”和“打倒某国人民”等表述。这些表述并未明确指向任何特定的友好国家。
3) 东三省是中国领土的一部分，中国政府至今仍视其为如此。尽管在东三省建立了所谓的“满洲国”，但中国政府并未承认其为一个正当的国家。该文章包含反“满洲国”的表述，但不能被视为构成违反促进与外国友好关系命令的行为。
4) 张季鸾是《大公报》的总编辑，事务繁忙。他不太关注报纸副刊栏目中的轻松文章。如果被指控的文章含有不当表述，被告张某虽应对此失误负责，但不能被视为故意违反刑法并危害和平与良好秩序。

September 11, 1936.    Morning

Ta Kung Pao:

"OUR NEWSPAPER PROSECUTED BY INTERNATIONAL SETTLEMENT
POLICE"

yesterday
At the First Special District Court/the Shanghai
Municipal Police charged Chang Chi Luan (張季鸞), editor
of our newspaper, with having endangered good order. Mr. Chang
attended.
The Municipal Advocate stated that on August 16,
the "Ta Kung Pao" published an article entitled "Plays That
Are Banned" which was regarded by the Police as being liable
to incite people to resist legal orders. The charge was
brought under Section 2, Article 153 of the Chinese Criminal
Code.
Mr. Chang, in the course of a statement, made
the following points:-
1) He is the man responsible for the editing of the "Ta
Kung Pao."
2) Great care is always exercised over all reports and
comments published in the "Ta Kung Pao."
3) The dramatic plays or novels published in the supplements
or in the section dealing with literary art come under
the category of amusements.
4) The literature referred to by the Municipal Advocate was
the manuscript of a dramatic play which contained nothing
of a nature liable to incite people to commit an offence.
5) As he has often been sick, it was possible that he might
not have paid sufficient attention to the articles in the
supplements.
He added that he did not know what the Police
meant by saying that the article was liable to incite people
to oppose legal orders.
Asked by the Judge as to where he had obtained
the manuscript of the article, Mr. Chang replied that the
article was contributed by some person whom he did not know.
The Municipal Advocate gave the following
explanations:- "The accused is charged with violation of
Section 2, Article 153 of the Chinese Criminal Code because
the article entitled 'Plays That Are Banned' refers to
'Manchukuo' and the nature of the play was liable to fan the
people's feelings over the North-East question. Thus it
constitutes an infringement of the orders promulgated by the
National Government on June 10 last year regarding the
promotion of friendly relations with foreign countries."
The accused then requested permission of the Judge
to express the following views:- "This newspaper has always
been careful when publishing any comments and reports; it
pays great attention to the promotion of friendly relations
with foreign countries and observance of government orders.
The Municipal Advocate now contends that a violation
of the Government orders had been committed because the
article published in the newspapers referred to 'Manchukuo'
and the Three North-Eastern Provinces. There must be some
misunderstanding. The Chinese Republic has never
relinquished its rights to the Three North-Eastern Provinces
and still regards them as Chinese territory. The National
Government has never recognized 'Manchukuo.' Therefore,

The Holmes (福尔摩斯) published the following article on September 11 :-

THE INDIAN MONEY-LENDERS

Most of the Indian residents in Shanghai are money-lenders. They usually employ special agents to find clients. They charge from 6 to 7% insterest per mensem. The borrower has to write out a promissory note in which the amount of the loan is not mentioned. Should a debtor fail to repay the money on the date due, the Indian money-lender would sue him in Court after filling in the blank space of the promissory note with the amount he thinks is due to him. For this reason, Judges, when dealing with such cases, usually act upon the terms of the promissory note with the result that borrowers from Indian money-lenders frequently suffer additional losses.
However, the Courts are now acquainted with this irregularity and have introduced a new method of dealing with such cases. In all such cases, the Courts will now examine the promissory note through a microscope to find out differences in the handwriting. The difference in colour of the ink is also an important factor.

yesterday
At the First Special District Court/the Shanghai

brought under Section 2, Article 153 of the Chinese Criminal

Mr. Chang, in the course of a statement, made
the following points:-
1) He is the man responsible for the editing of the "Ta

2) Great care is always exercised over all reports and

3) The dramatic plays or novels published in the supplements

National Government on June 10 last year regarding the

been careful when publishing any comments and reports; it

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

GOLD FISH MERCHANT INJURED BY JAPANESE MARINE

Wong Sz Han (王時漢), age 26, residing in a hut on Pingliang Road in the Eastern District, is the proprietor of the Chien Zung Gold Fish Shop (泉成) on Pingliang Road.
At 5.30 p.m. September 16, two Japanese marines were admitted to view the fish pond. After a while, the marines entered Wong's sleeping room, took out a wash basin and selected more than ten gold fish from the pond. When Wong asked the marines for payment, the marines replied that they had no money. A dispute arose in the course of which Wong took back the wash basin from the hands of a marine and poured the fish back into the pond. The other marine then drew his bayonet and stabbed Wong in the left leg. Upon seeing his condition, the Japanese marines took Wong to the Japanese primary school at the corner of Pingliang and Ningkuo Roads with the object of dressing his wound. Wong was not satisfied. At this stage, a foreign Policeman No. 90 of Yangtsepoo Police Station, who happened to pass by, took Wong to the Sacred Heart Hospital for treatment. In the evening, Wong attended at Yangtsepoo Station for interrogation.
On the morning of September 17, the Japanese Naval Landing Headquarters and the Japanese Consulate sent officers to the shop to make an investigation. The Japanese marine who created the trouble was also present. A photograph was taken by the Japanese officials.
Last night, our reporter visited the shop. Wong had returned home. His injuries are not serious. Wong said that when he was interrogated at the Police Station, the two Japanese marines were not there. His loss has not yet been made good.

The other day, the Shanghai Municipal Police prosecuted our paper in the First Shanghai Special District Court for having published an article entitled "Plays That Are Banned", which was regarded as an infringement of the order of the National Government for the promotion of good relations with foreign countries.

金鱼商被日本海军陆战队员刺伤

王时汉（Wong Sz Han），26岁，居住在东区平凉路的一间棚屋内，是平凉路上泉成金鱼店（Chien Zung Gold Fish Shop）的店主。
9月16日下午5时30分，两名日本海军陆战队员进入店内观看鱼池。过了一会儿，陆战队员进入王的卧室，拿出一个脸盆，从池中挑选了十多条金鱼。当王要求陆战队员付款时，陆战队员回答说他们没有钱。双方发生争执，期间王从一名陆战队员手中夺回脸盆，将鱼倒回池中。另一名陆战队员随即拔出刺刀，刺伤了王的左腿。日本陆战队员见其状况，将王带到平凉路与宁国路拐角处的日本小学，目的是为其包扎伤口。王对此不满意。此时，恰巧路过的杨树浦巡捕房第90号外籍巡捕将王送往圣心医院治疗。晚上，王前往杨树浦巡捕房接受讯问。
9月17日上午，日本海军登陆司令部和日本领事馆派官员到店进行调查。肇事的那名日本陆战队员也在场。日本官员拍了照片。
昨晚，本报记者走访了该店。王已回家。他的伤势并不严重。王说，他在巡捕房接受讯问时，那两名日本陆战队员不在场。他的损失尚未得到赔偿。

《大公报》：-

针对本报的案件被驳回

September 16, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Shanghai Kwangtung Pao ( 上海廣東報 ) published the following
comment on September 15 :-

"PLAYS THAT ARE BANNED"

China has not yet been conquered, yet her
people are living like slaves. Nothing is done when the
people of one of our friendly nations kill one of our
brethren, but when we kill a member of one of our friendly
nations, it becomes a big affair.
The prohibition by the S.M.C. of the staging
of the play entitled "The Smuggling" by the Zuh Nyi ( 突販 )
Dramatic Group created a deep, painful impression upon the
minds of the Chinese people. Now the "Ta Kung Pao" is
being prosecuted for having violated the order of the
National Government for the promotion of good relations
with foreign countries.
During the hearing of the case, the editor
of the "Ta Kung Pao" said: "The Chinese Government still
regards the Three Eastern Provinces as part of its territory;
the Government has not recognized Manchukuo. Therefore,
Manchukuo is not one of the friendly nations referred to
in the order for the promotion of good relations with foreign
countries."
The territory of China has been seized by
others. Are the Chinese not to be allowed to cherish a
hope of recovering the lost territory?
Great Britain is sending 10,000 soldiers to
Palestine to suppress uprisings there although it is not
British territory. The Three Eastern Provinces are part
of the territory of China.

1936年9月16日。下午译文。

《上海廣東報》于9月15日刊登如下评论：-

“被禁演的戏剧”

中国尚未被征服，但其人民却过着奴隶般的生活。当一个友好国家的国民杀害我们的同胞时，当局无所作为；但当我们要杀害一个友好国家的成员时，却成了大事。
公共租界工部局禁止“突販”（Zuh Nyi，音译）剧团上演名为《走私》的戏剧，在中国民众心中留下了深刻而痛苦的印象。如今，《大公報》因违反国民政府关于促进与外国良好关系的命令而受到起诉。
在案件审理期间，《大公報》编辑称：“中国政府仍将东三省视为其领土的一部分；政府并未承认满洲国。因此，满洲国并非促进与外国友好关系命令中所指的友好国家之一。”
中国的领土已被他人攫取。难道不允许中国人怀有收复失地的希望吗？
英国正向巴勒斯坦派遣一万名士兵以镇压那里的起义，尽管巴勒斯坦并非英国领土。东三省是中国领土的一部分。

The Iron News (铁板) published the following brief comment
on September 13 :-

"PLAYS THAT ARE BANNED"

The S.M.P. has charged the "Ta Kung Pao"
with publishing an article entitled "Plays That Are Banned"
which refers to the Three Eastern Provinces and "Manchukuo",
because it violates the order of the National Government
for the promotion of good relations with foreign countries.
Is "Manchukuo" a friendly nation? Do we
offend our friendly nation, Japan, which is doing her best
to promote peace in East Asia, whenever we talk of
"Manchukuo"?
The Chinese authorities have not recognized
"Manchukuo". Furthermore, General Chiang Kai Shek has said
that when others should insist upon our recognition of
"Manchukuo", the time had come to offer resistance.
Let us see how the Court will decide the
case.

NICHINICHI

EDITOR OF THE "TA KUNG PAO" PROSECUTED BY THE
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

In publishing a translation
of an article appearing in the September 11 issue of the
"Ta Kung Pao" concerning the prosecution of the editor of
the newspaper by the Shanghai Municipal Police, the Nichi-
Nichi states that attention is being paid to the judgement
to be given by the Court on September 17 as it will constitute
a precedent for future procedure.

Ta Sung Pao (大公报) published the following comment on Sept.12:-

"PLAYS THAT ARE BANNED"

The "Ta Kung Pao" is being prosecuted by the S.M.P.
in the First Shanghai Special District Court for having
published an article entitled "Plays That Are Banned" on
the ground that the article is liable to incite the people's
feelings over the Three Eastern Provinces question and
that it also refers to "Manchukuo". The article was
regarded as having infringed the orders of the National
Government for the promotion of good relations with foreign
countries.
The orders of the National Government for the
promotion of good relations with foreign countries refer
to independent countries. As for the so-called "Manchukuo",
it is but an imperfect organization. China still regards
the territory of "Manchukuo" as her territory. Furthermore,
Great Britain, America and other foreign countries, except
Japan, have not recognized "Manchukuo" as an independent
State. Therefore, the S.M.P. seems to have misunderstood
the orders of the National Government. In our opinion,
the "Ta Kung Pao" is not guilty.
It is learned that judgment in the case will
be delivered on September 17. Let us wait and see how
the case will be decided.

《铁板》于9月13日刊登如下简短评论：-

“被禁演的戏剧”

公共租界警务处指控《大公報》发表了一篇题为《被禁演的戏剧》的文章，文中提及东三省和“满洲国”，因其违反了国民政府关于促进与外国良好关系的命令。
“满洲国”是友好国家吗？每当我们谈论“满洲国”时，是否就冒犯了尽力促进东亚和平的友好国家日本？
中国当局并未承认“满洲国”。此外，蒋介石将军曾表示，当他人坚持要求我们承认“满洲国”时，便是进行抵抗之时。
让我们看看法庭将如何裁决此案。

《日日新闻》（NICHINICHI）

《大公報》编辑遭上海公共租界警务处起诉

《日日新闻》在翻译刊登9月11日《大公報》有关该报编辑被上海公共租界警务处起诉的文章时指出，人们正关注法庭将于9月17日作出的判决，因为该判决将成为未来诉讼程序的先例。

《大公报》（Ta Sung Pao，注：此处原文拼写可能有误，结合上下文应指另一家报纸或为《大公報》之异写，依指令保留原文拼音对应汉字，但鉴于前文已有《大公報》，此处按音译处理或依常见报刊名推测，若不确定则保留。根据历史背景，Ta Sung Pao 可能指《大松报》或为 OCR 错误，但指令要求不确定保留原文加音译。然而 Ta Kung Pao 已译为大公報。此处 Ta Sung Pao 可能是另一家报纸。暂按音译处理，或若确认为同一报纸则统一。经查证，当时并无著名《大松报》，极可能是《大公報》的另一种拼写错误或另一小报。遵照指令“不确定的保留原文并加括号注明(音译)”，但 Ta Kung Pao 已确定。此处 Ta Sung Pao 与 Ta Kung Pao 拼写不同，故视为不同实体或错误。若视为错误，应照实译出。此处译为《大松报》(音译) 以示区别，或若认为是同一报纸的笔误，考虑到语境完全一致，极大概率是同一报纸。但为了严谨遵循“不确定保留原文”，这里处理为：《大松报》(Ta Sung Pao，音译)。*修正：根据历史档案习惯，有时同一报纸有不同拼写。但既然前文已定 Ta Kung Pao 为《大公報》，此处 Ta Sung Pao 若无法确定即为《大公報》，则按音译。*) 

*注：经再次审视，Ta Sung Pao 极有可能是 Ta Kung Pao 的 OCR 识别错误或打字错误，因为评论内容完全承接上文。但在严格遵循指令下，若不能100%确定是同一报纸（尽管可能性极大），应谨慎。不过，通常 Ta Kung Pao 即《大公報》。此处 Ta Sung Pao 很可能是《大公報》的误植。若必须翻译，且不确定，则：*

《大松报》(Ta Sung Pao，音译) 于9月12日刊登如下评论：-

“被禁演的戏剧”

《大公報》因在上海第一特区地方法院被公共租界警务处起诉，理由是其发表了一篇题为《被禁演的戏剧》的文章，据称该文章容易激起民众对东三省问题的情绪，并且提及了“满洲国”。该文章被视为侵犯了国民政府关于促进与外国良好关系的命令。
国民政府关于促进与外国良好关系的命令指的是独立国家。至于所谓的“满洲国”，它只是一个不完备的组织。中国仍视“满洲国”的领土为其领土。此外，除日本外，英国、美国及其他外国均未承认“满洲国”为独立国家。因此，公共租界警务处似乎误解了国民政府的命令。我们认为，《大公報》无罪。
据悉，该案判决将于9月17日宣判。让我们拭目以待此案将如何裁决。

September 11, 1936.
Morning Translation.

Ta Kung Pao:

"OUR NEWSPAPER PROSECUTED BY INTERNATIONAL SETTLEMENT
POLICE"

yesterday
At the First Special District Court/the Shanghai
Municipal Police charged Chang Chi Luan (張季鸞), editor
of our newspaper, with having endangered good order. Mr. Chang
attended.

The Municipal Advocate stated that on August 16,
the "Ta Kung Pao" published an article entitled "Plays That
Are Banned" which was regarded by the Police as being liable
to incite people to resist legal orders. The charge was
brought under Section 2, Article 153 of the Chinese Criminal
Code.

Mr. Chang, in the course of a statement, made
the following points:-
1) He is the man responsible for the editing of the "Ta
Kung Pao."
2) Great care is always exercised over all reports and
comments published in the "Ta Kung Pao."
3) The dramatic plays or novels published in the supplements
or in the section dealing with literary art come under
the category of amusements.
4) The literature referred to by the Municipal Advocate was
the manuscript of a dramatic play which contained nothing
of a nature liable to incite people to commit an offence.
5) As he has often been sick, it was possible that he might
not have paid sufficient attention to the articles in the
supplements.

He added that he did not know what the Police
meant by saying that the article was liable to incite people
to oppose legal orders.

Asked by the Judge as to where he had obtained
the manuscript of the article, Mr. Chang replied that the
article was contributed by some person whom he did not know.

The Municipal Advocate gave the following
explanation:- "The accused is charged with violation of
Section 2, Article 153 of the Chinese Criminal Code because
the article entitled 'Plays That Are Banned' refers to
'Manchukuo' and the nature of the play was liable to fan the
people's feelings over the North-East question. Thus it
constitutes an infringement of the orders promulgated by the
National Government on June 10 last year regarding the
promotion of friendly relations with foreign countries."

The accused then requested permission of the Judge
to express the following views:- "This newspaper has always
been careful when publishing any comments and reports; it
pays great attention to the promotion of friendly relations
with foreign countries and observance of government orders.
The Municipal Advocate now contends that a violation
of the Government orders had been committed because the
article published in the newspapers referred to 'Manchukuo'
and the Three North-Eastern Provinces. There must be some
misunderstanding. The Chinese Republic has never
relinquished its rights to the Three North-Eastern Provinces
and still regards them as Chinese territory. The National
Government has never recognized 'Manchukuo.' Therefore,
'Manchukuo' does not come within the category of so-called
friendly nations as mentioned in the Government's orders."

The lawyer for the defence stated that the charge
had no legal basis. The Judge announced that a decision
would be delivered next Thursday.

1936年9月11日。
晨间译件。

《大公报》：

“本报遭公共租界警方起诉”

昨日
在第一特区法院，上海公共租界工部局警务处指控本报总编辑张季鸾危害治安。张先生出庭应诉。

公诉人陈述称，8月16日，《大公报》刊登了一篇题为《禁戏》的文章，警方认为该文有可能煽动民众抗拒法令。此项指控依据《中华民国刑法》第一百五十三条第二款提出。

张先生在陈述中提出了以下几点：
1) 他是负责《大公报》编辑工作的人。
2) 《大公报》刊登的所有报道和评论均经过审慎处理。
3) 副刊或文艺栏目中刊登的戏剧或小说属于娱乐范畴。
4) 公诉人所指的文学作品是一出戏剧的手稿，其中不包含任何可能煽动民众犯罪的内容。
5) 由于他经常患病，可能未对副刊中的文章给予足够关注。

他补充说，他不明白警方所谓文章可能煽动民众反对合法命令是何含义。

法官询问该文章手稿的来源时，张先生回答说，该文章是由一位他不认识的人士投稿的。

公诉人作出如下解释：“被告被控违反《中华民国刑法》第一百五十三条第二款，因为题为《禁戏》的文章提及‘满洲国’，且该剧的性质有可能激起民众对东北问题的情绪。因此，这构成了对去年6月10日国民政府颁布的关于促进与外国友好关系的命令的侵犯。”

随后，被告请求法官允许其表达以下观点：“本报在刊登任何评论和报道时一向谨慎；高度重视促进与外国的友好关系并遵守政府命令。公诉人现在声称，由于报纸刊登的文章提及‘满洲国’及东北三省，因而违反了政府命令。这其中必定存在某种误解。中华共和国从未放弃对东北三省的权利，仍将其视为中国领土。国民政府从未承认‘满洲国’。因此，‘满洲国’不属于政府命令中所谓的友好国家范畴。”

辩护律师表示，该项指控缺乏法律依据。法官宣布将于下周四宣判。

PLAYS THAT ARE BANNED.

Time: 2 p.m. on a certain day of June, 1936.
Scene: The back stage of a certain theatre.
A rehearsal is going on.

Wei: Lord, I am a native of "Manchukuo". Have
pity on me as I have only this son. Release
him, my Lord.
Chen (opening the manuscript and reading): No. He is
anti-"Manchukuo". You want to start a
revolution. I shall cut off your head.
Lan: We shall kill you, you XX devil; we shall
kill you, you XX devil. Brothers! Come and
kill him!
Chang (after putting on the military uniform of the soldier
of a certain nation): You, Miss Chi Na (China).
I love you.
Miss Wong (striking him with a whip): You small devil.
Chang (running to the rear): How fierce the girl of
Chi Na is!
Lan (kicking Chang in the buttocks): Overthrow, overthrow,
overthrow the people of a certain nation.
Chang: You are very fierce in assaulting me, an
imitation devil of a certain nation. Are
you equally bold as to go to.......
Yih (the director): Let us stage the play at once.
Detectives have already come, saying that they
would examine our plays. Raise the curtain
as soon as possible in order to avoid trouble.
It is now ten minutes before the time fixed
for the play. Where is Miss Chang Tse?

(Enter Chang Tse, with face pale)
Chang Tse: Director Yih, I cannot act in the performance.
My father has been killed by the soldiers of a
certain nation. He resided in Shenyang; he
was anti-"Manchukuo". For this reason, he
has been shot. (Covering her face and beginning
to weep). I am going at once to Peiping by the
Peiping-Shanghai through train and from there
I shall go to the North-East. I want to avenge
his death.
Yih: Miss Chang, you should regard your revenge
as an act for the whole Chinese race. I hope
you can act in the performance.
Chang Tse (angrily): I shall play in "The Night of
Shenyang". I am now going to change my dress
for the stage.

Curtain rises and the performance begins.
Suddenly a whistle is heard. Yih, the director,

Yih: The play entitled "The Night of Shenyang" is prohibited. A foreign detective says that this play endangers the good relations with foreign countries because the play has a character representing the people of XX nations; furthermore, the play contains the expression "The North-East belongs to China."

In the past, we escaped to the south and thought we could carry out a part of the national salvation work through the stage. Now plays are not allowed to be staged in the south. In the North-East, others are slaughtering our people day and night with aeroplanes and guns. What is the use of shouting slogans here? This bloody enmity can only be cleared by blood. The 'Ta Kung Pao' (l'Impartial), a leading Chinese
daily newspaper in Tientsin, started to publish the Shanghai
edition on April 1, 1936.
The cause is due to the fact that the paper was
recently banned by order of the Hopei-Chahar Political Council
for publishing editorials denouncing the Council on the Sino-
Japanese affairs. The ban was subsequently removed by order
of the National Government. At first it was proposed to
remove the office of the paper from Tientsin to Shanghai, but
finally it was resolved to publish another newspaper in
Shanghai under the same name.
Ho Tseng Ts (胡政之) and Tsang Kee Lou (張季鸞),
Publisher and Editor-in-Chief of the paper respectively, are
now editing the papers in Tientsin and Shanghai by rotation,
i.e. if Ho works at Tientsin this month, Tsang should stay
in Shanghai and vice versa. Both are friends of Mr. Kawagoe,
Japanese Ambassador to China.
The Shanghai Office of the paper is at Nos.161/181
Avenue Edward VII with a sales office at No.436 Foochow Road.
Feng Su Lou (馮叔鸞), a well-known journalist,
who was one of secretaries to the Bureau of Public Safety in
1935, and Li Tae Kwei (李子寬), Manager of the Kuo Wen News
Agency, are Manager and Assistant Manager of the paper
respectively.
About 45,000 copies are printed daily but the
circulation is poor; it has to sustain a heavy loss monthly.

先生，
《大公报》（l'Impartial），天津的一家主要中文日报，于1936年4月1日开始出版上海版。
原因是该报近期因刊登社论谴责冀察政务委员会在中日事务上的做法，而被冀察政务委员会下令查禁。随后，国民政府下令解除查禁。起初提议将报社从天津迁至上海，但最终决定在上海以同一名称出版另一份报纸。
该报的出版人胡政之（Ho Tseng Ts）和总编辑张季鸾（Tsang Kee Lou / 張季鸞），目前轮流在天津和上海编辑报纸，即如果本月胡在天津工作，张就应留在上海，反之亦然。两人都是日本驻华大使川越茂（Kawagoe）先生的朋友。
该报上海办事处位于爱德华七世路161/181号，并在福州路436号设有销售处。
著名记者冯叔鸾（Feng Su Lou），曾于1935年担任公安局秘书之一，以及国闻通讯社经理李子宽（Li Tae Kwei），分别担任该报的经理和副经理。
